description:
Dein Netzwerk reicht vom Leitstand bis in die Vorstandsetage? In Energie und Industrie kennt man dich, und wenn irgendwo ein Cloud- oder KI-Projekt ansteht, klingelt zuerst dein Telefon? Dann lass uns reden.

Wir suchen genau dich, wenn du bei einem IT-Dienstleister oder Beratungshaus Lösungen in Data, KI, Cloud und Kubernetes verkauft hast. Keine Köpfe, sondern Projekte, die beim Kunden den Unterschied machen.

Pexon Consulting baut Cloud- und KI-Plattformen für große Unternehmen und den gehobenen Mittelstand im DACH-Raum. Seit 2020 haben wir über 400 Projekte umgesetzt, für mehr als 100 Kunden. Wir sind Partner von AWS, Microsoft Azure und Google Cloud und nach ISO 27001 zertifiziert. Unser Versprechen: Bankqualität und KI auf Kubernetes.

Du baust mit uns das Key Account Management für Energie und Industrie auf. Du arbeitest direkt mit Geschäftsführung und Vertriebsleitung zusammen und mit unseren Principals für AI, Data, Document Intelligence und Cloud/Kubernetes.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Deine Key Accounts: Du verantwortest ausgewählte Key Accounts in Energie und Industrie. Bei Neukunden treibst du nach dem ersten Projekt Upselling und Cross-Selling.

  • Beziehungen aufbauen: Du führst Feedback-, Kennenlern- und Jahresgespräche. Du lernst neue Ansprechpartner in IT, Fachbereich und Geschäftsführung kennen und hältst die Stakeholder-Map aktuell.

  • Chancen erkennen: Aus jedem Gespräch und jedem Projektende machst du konkrete Ideen für das nächste Projekt. Du schließt sie gemeinsam mit unseren Principals ab.

  • Große Accounts gemeinsam: In unseren wichtigsten Kunden sprichst du zusammen mit der Vertriebsleitung mehr Bereiche und Entscheider an.

  • Neue Türen öffnen: Du gehst gezielt auf Bereiche und Standorte unserer Kunden zu, die uns noch nicht kennen.

  • Events: Du planst Kundenevents mit, zum Beispiel Executive Round Tables und Dinner, und bist auf den wichtigen Branchenevents in Energie und Industrie präsent.

  • Du steuerst selbst: Du verantwortest deine Aktivitäten, deine Pipeline und deinen Forecast und machst transparent, wo du stehst.

Was wir dir bieten

  • Gehaltspaket: Ein attraktives Gehalt und Boni, die nach oben offen sind.

  • Echte Kunden statt Kaltakquise: Du startest mit Accounts, die uns schon kennen, und mit Principals, die liefern können.

  • Projekte, die Spaß machen: Wir arbeiten an richtig spannenden Cloud- und KI-Projekten für namhafte Kunden aus Energie, Industrie und Finanzen.

  • Ein Markt mit Zukunft: Cloud, Data und KI gehören zu den Themen, die in den nächsten Jahren am stärksten wachsen. Du bist von Anfang an dabei.

  • Kurze Wege: Du arbeitest direkt mit der Geschäftsführung zusammen. Ideen werden schnell entschieden und umgesetzt.

  • Entwicklung: Wir wachsen stark. Wer mitzieht, wächst mit, in Verantwortung, Accounts und Team.

  • Flexibilität: Du arbeitest von zu Hause oder in unserem Büro in München.

  • Extras: Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Wellpass, Zuschuss zum Mittagessen jeden Tag, MacBook Pro und aktuelle Software.

  • Erfahrung: Mindestens 4 Jahre Account Management oder Vertrieb von IT-Dienstleistungen, idealerweise in einem IT-Beratungshaus. Cloud, Data oder KI hast du schon verkauft, Bodyleasing reicht nicht.

  • Haltung: Du fragst nach, hörst zu und bleibst dran. Ein „Nein“ heute ist für dich der Start für das nächste Gespräch.

  • Rahmen: Deutsch fließend, Englisch gut und Lust auf Kundentermine vor Ort, etwa zwei bis drei Tage im Monat.

About the Role

Our reps spend most of their day in Salesforce, and how it feels to use directly affects how much they sell. We're hiring a Salesforce Developer with a UI/UX focus to redesign the rep experience across our Sales and Revenue teams. You'll join the global Salesforce team for 12 months to make the CRM faster, clearer and more intuitive.

This is a hands-on build role. You'll design the experience and code it in Lightning Web Components, working with Sales, RevOps, Marketing and Data, and directly with the reps who use the result.


What You Will Do


Redesign the rep experience

  • Audit the current Lightning experience (record pages, console apps, list views, home pages) and find where reps lose time to clicks, clutter and missing context.

  • Turn what you find into a prioritised roadmap of UI improvements tied to rep productivity and adoption.

  • Design and prototype improved layouts, workflows and components, and validate them with reps before building.

Build with LWC

  • Develop custom Lightning Web Components (and supporting Apex where needed) that replace clunky standard layouts with focused, usable interfaces.

  • Configure and extend Lightning App Builder pages, Dynamic Forms, Dynamic Actions and console apps to deliver a consistent experience across teams and regions.

  • Build reusable components and follow SLDS conventions so the UI stays consistent and maintainable after your contract ends.

Make it stick

  • Run feedback sessions, usability tests and pilots with reps and managers, and iterate on the results.

  • Track adoption, page performance and user satisfaction to show what each release changed.

  • Create release notes, short walkthroughs and handover documentation so changes land well and the team can maintain what you build.

Work as part of the global team

  • Work within the global team's standards for source control, code review, sandboxes and release management.

  • Partner with admins, architects and data teams so UI changes fit the wider data model, security model and automation.

  • Pass on what you learn about Lightning UX patterns and LWC best practices to the wider team.


What You Will Need


Must have

  • Strong, demonstrable experience building Lightning Web Components in production.

  • Solid Apex, SOQL and Salesforce data model knowledge to support your components.

  • Deep knowledge of Lightning Experience customisation: App Builder, Dynamic Forms, page layouts, console apps and Flows.

  • Experience with Salesforce DX, Git and a CI/CD or deployment process.

  • A UX mindset: you start from user problems, can explain design decisions, and can take feedback from non-technical users.

  • Clear communication and the ability to work independently across time zones in a global team.

Nice to have

  • Portfolio or examples of Salesforce UI work you've shipped (screenshots or demos are ideal).

  • Experience with SLDS, Figma or similar prototyping tools, and accessibility (WCAG) principles.

  • Experience in Sales Cloud, especially rep-facing workflows such as opportunity management, account planning and pipeline views.

  • Jest testing for LWC, and Salesforce certifications (Platform Developer I/II, JavaScript Developer I, Platform App Builder).

  • Experience with performance profiling and optimisation in Lightning pages.


What Success Looks Like (12 Months)

  • Month 3: UX audit complete and a prioritised roadmap agreed with Sales leadership.

  • Month 6: First wave of redesigned pages and components live for a pilot group, with adoption and feedback baselined.

  • Month 12: Redesigned experience rolled out to target teams, a maintained component library in place, and full documentation handed to the global team.

What we offer

  • Your choice of perk: a gym membership (Urban Sports Club) or a BVG public transport ticket.

  • Relocation support to help you move seamlessly into one of our hubs.

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work

We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

About Valova

We are building the AI operations platform for European hospitals, so every clinician can focus on patients.

Behind every patient sits a chain of admin work: documentation, coding, billing, audits, scheduling. It runs through disconnected systems and endless manual hand-offs, while most German hospitals already operate at a loss.

We start where the impact is measurable from day one: case to cash. Valova codes every case, defends it in audits and makes sure the money lands. From there we take on every workflow that runs a hospital, until one agentic system handles the routine and people decide the exceptions. First Germany, then Europe.

Doctors, engineers and operators, on-site in Munich and Berlin. Join us!

Why this role matters

Our agents are the product. Every case Valova codes runs through agentic systems that read clinical documentation, apply coding rules and justify every decision. How accurate, how fast and how efficient these systems are decides how much revenue hospitals recover and how much time coders get back. As AI/ML Engineer, you own the core of Valova: the agents that turn long, unstructured German clinical documentation into codes a hospital can bill and defend. You decide how we combine large and small models, how we measure quality and how new research makes it into production within weeks, not quarters.

Your impact is directly measurable: in coding accuracy, in token costs per case and in hospitals that trust every decision because they can trace it.

This is a hands-on engineering role building AI systems in production with real users. It’s not academic research, and it’s not prompt tinkering on the side of a product others build.

How the role sits in the team

You report directly to Christian, our CTO, and work day to day with our engineering team on the agent pipeline, infrastructure and evaluation. With Malte and our product team, you translate what is technically possible into product decisions. Our doctors and coding experts are your sparring partners for clinical quality, and our forward deployed team brings back how the agents perform in real hospitals.

Du berichtest direkt an Christian, unseren CTO, und arbeitest täglich mit unserem Engineering-Team an der Agenten-Pipeline, der Infrastruktur und der Evaluation. Mit Malte und unserem Produktteam übersetzt Du, was technisch möglich ist, in Produktentscheidungen. Unsere Ärzt:innen und Kodierexpert:innen sind Deine Sparringspartner für klinische Qualität, und unser Forward-Deployed-Team bringt zurück, wie die Agenten in echten Kliniken performen.

What you will do

  • Build state-of-the-art agents: You build high-performing agentic systems that define the state of the art in healthcare text processing, while staying efficient in token usage and leveraging small models wherever possible.

  • Make every decision traceable: You ensure every decision and output of our agents is traced, and you monitor their performance in production.

  • Measure what matters: You build the evaluation and benchmarking setup that tells us, on every change, whether our agents got better or worse.

  • Bring research to production: You follow new AI/ML approaches, benchmark promising ideas and make sure the best results reach production within weeks.

  • Shape the product: You use your AI/ML expertise to evaluate future projects and inform product decisions.

What we are looking for:

  • Production experience: At least two years building and shipping ML/AI systems in production.

  • LLM and agent expertise: Strong experience with LLMs and agentic frameworks.

  • Engineering depth: Strong proficiency in your primary programming language.

  • Evaluation mindset: Experience with observability, evaluation and benchmarking of ML systems.

  • Product mindset: You care about outcomes that lead to great user experiences and are passionate about using LLMs in real-world scenarios rather than academic research.

  • Nice to have: Experience in healthcare, regulated environments or with sensitive data.

  • Languages: You speak fluent English. German is a big plus, since the clinical documents our agents process are in German.

  • Location: You work from our office in Munich or Berlin.

Missing one or two points, but convinced you’re the right person for this role? Apply anyway. We’re looking forward to meeting you!

What you get

  • Work that means something, every day. Your agents are the core of our product and directly help improve the German healthcare system.

  • Ownership from week one. You take over real projects with a clear outcome and your name on it, not a list of tasks someone else defined.

  • Direct access to the founders. You work day to day with our founders Sophia, a physician and ex-McKinsey consultant, and Christian, who has founded two health tech startups and spent a decade building clinical systems. No layers, no waiting weeks for approvals.

  • Trust and freedom. We trust you to solve problems your way, and the team has your back 100%.

  • Learning at startup speed. You will see more in one year here than in three years elsewhere, across models, infrastructure, product and customers, with a team that has a proven track record of deploying AI in healthcare.

  • One team, in the heart of the city. We work together on-site at WeWork Odeonsplatz in Munich and WeWork in central Berlin. Fully serviced offices with coffee, meeting rooms and phone booths mean zero admin, and the city-center location means short commutes, easy access to customers and investors, and lunch spots around every corner.

  • Team events that bring Munich and Berlin together, because the people you build with should also be the people you celebrate with.

What success looks like

  • After 3 months, you know our agent pipeline inside out, every agent decision is traced, and you have shipped your first improvement to production.

  • After 6 months, our evaluation and benchmarking setup runs on every change, and you have measurably improved coding quality or reduced token costs per case.

  • After 12 months, at least one new approach from research is running in production, and parts of our pipeline run on smaller models without losing quality.

  • Throughout, our AI-related product decisions are grounded in your benchmarks, and the team turns to you when a new model or method comes out.

How it works

Just upload your CV with your application. We’ll get in touch with you for the next steps:

  1. Intro call (30 min): We get to know each other, talk about your background and answer your first questions.

  2. Technical interview with Christian (CTO) (60 min): We dive into the ML/AI systems you’ve built and how you evaluated them in production.

  3. Case: You design an agentic approach for a realistic clinical coding problem, including how you would evaluate it, and present it to the team.

  4. References: We speak with two or three people you’ve worked with, such as former managers or colleagues.

  5. Meet the team: You spend a day with us on-site in Munich or Berlin, meet our founders Sophia and Christian and see how we work day to day.

  6. Offer: If it’s a match for both sides, you’ll hear from us quickly.

We look forward to your application, regardless of gender, background, religion, disability, age or sexual identity.

title: Software engineer, AI model supply chain and package security
description:
We build fast, modern developer tools in Rust, and a surprising amount of serious software runs on them. Pixi, rattler and rattler-build are open source and used by hundreds of thousands of developers: quant teams in finance, physicists at CERN, biotech labs, and humanoid robot companies you've probably seen videos of. We are also core maintainers of conda-forge, one of the largest open source package ecosystems, and we maintain RoboStack, which gets ROS running on any OS from a single lockfile.

When that much software flows through your tools, security stops being optional. Every package that ends up on a laptop, a server or a robot should be traceable back to the source and build that produced it. We're building that for conda today, and we want to extend it to AI models.

The engineering team is spread across Europe (Netherlands, Germany, UK, Moldova). This work is based in Berlin, and so is this role.

The work

Robots increasingly run learned models: vision transformers, RL policies, LLMs. Today those models are usually copied onto machines as large opaque files, with little record of where they came from or what changed. We think models should be shipped like packages: versioned, signed, verifiable, and updated efficiently.

You'll work on two related areas.

Package security. Signing and verification for conda packages with Sigstore, provenance from source to build to install, SBOMs, and mapping known vulnerabilities onto the packages people actually use. This work goes into Pixi, rattler and conda-forge, and is used by a lot of people.

AI models as packages. Taking the same ideas to model artifacts. That includes:

  • A provenance chain from training through packaging to deployment, with signatures that can be verified offline on air-gapped robots

  • A model SBOM format, building on CycloneDX's ML-BOM

  • Delta updates between model versions (full models, fine-tunes, LoRA adapters, quantized variants), so robots don't download gigabytes for a small change

  • Compression that combines model techniques (quantization, pruning, distillation) with what package managers already do well (zstd, content-addressable storage), tuned to the target hardware and network

  • Managing models that get fine-tuned on the robot itself: tracking where those variants came from, validating them, and syncing them back

  • Testing the whole pipeline end to end on real models and real hardware, and measuring latency, bandwidth and model quality

A lot of this is new. Part of the job is figuring out which approaches work, measuring them honestly, and writing up what you found.

What we're looking for

You don't need years of experience. You do need solid fundamentals, curiosity, and the patience to get security details right.

  • Rust, or a strong background in C++, Go or Python and the wish to switch

  • Interest in software supply chain security. Bonus if you've worked with Sigstore (Cosign, Rekor, Fulcio), TUF, in-toto, SLSA or SBOM formats

  • Familiarity with ML in practice: you've trained or fine-tuned a model, know what a LoRA adapter or a quantized model is, and have used PyTorch or similar

  • Basic understanding of cryptography as an engineer: signatures, hashes, certificates, and what they do and don't guarantee

  • You like measuring things and are honest about results that don't work out

  • You live in Berlin or are willing to move here

It's a plus if you know package managers from the inside, have worked on model compression or edge inference, have robotics experience, or have contributed to open source. None of this is required.

What we offer

You'll work on problems few people have solved yet, together with the people who created Mamba, Pixi, rattler and RoboStack. Most of your work will be open source and used by a large community from day one. We pay a competitive Berlin salary, with 30 days of vacation, the hardware you want, a conference budget, and time for upstream open source work. We help with relocation within the EU.
